boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on practical campus-adjacent Honolulu corridors, with one source-supported reason to stop at each.

cards.title: Nijiya Market University Store
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the University Avenue stop to browse the Japanese grocery selection; confirm current hours before making a specific trip.
cards.short_summary: Japanese grocery stop at 1009 University Ave.
cards.evidence_claim: Nijiya lists its University Store at 1009 University Ave., Honolulu, with daily 9 a.m.–9 p.m. hours.
cards.access_notes: The official location page lists daily hours; holiday hours differ.

cards.title: Island Brew Coffeehouse Mānoa
cards.subtitle: University Avenue at Metcalf Street
cards.notes: Meet beside the University–Metcalf corner for coffee and food; use the shop’s ordering page to confirm service availability.
cards.short_summary: Coffeehouse in the RISE Center’s historic Charles Atherton Building.
cards.evidence_claim: UH reports Island Brew occupies a ground-floor space in the Charles Atherton Building with frontage at Metcalf Street and University Avenue.
cards.source_title: Mānoa: Island Brew Coffeehouse to open in Walter Dods, Jr. RISE Center
cards.access_notes: The business ordering page identifies the Mānoa location as 1810 University Avenue.

cards.title: Oli's Kitchen
cards.subtitle: University Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Take the University Avenue entrance into the parking lot, then check the restaurant’s direct ordering page for the current menu.
cards.short_summary: Hawaiian comfort-food kitchen at 1009 University Ave.
cards.evidence_claim: Oli’s Kitchen identifies its location as MP2, 1009 University Ave., Honolulu, and describes its Hawaiian comfort-food menu.
cards.access_notes: Enter the lot between Kansai Yamato and Betty’s Burgers, as directed by the business.

cards.title: Down to Earth Honolulu
cards.subtitle: South King Street near University Avenue
cards.notes: Stop for natural and organic groceries or the deli, then use the official store page for current department and parking details.
cards.short_summary: Natural-food store with grocery, deli, and prepared-food departments.
cards.evidence_claim: Down to Earth lists its Honolulu store at 2525 S King St near University Avenue and describes grocery, produce, bulk-food, and deli offerings.
cards.source_title: Down to Earth Organic & Natural — Honolulu, Oahu
cards.access_notes: Official page lists a free parking garage and metered street parking.

cards.title: McCully-Mōʻiliʻili Public Library
cards.subtitle: South King Street corridor
cards.notes: Use this named South King Street public-library stop for a structured reading or study visit; check the state system for program updates.
cards.short_summary: State public library at 2211 S King St.
cards.evidence_claim: A State of Hawaiʻi library-system document identifies McCully-Mōʻiliʻili Public Library at 2211 S King St., Honolulu.
cards.source_title: Hawaiʻi State Public Library System budget testimony
cards.access_notes: Confirm current branch hours and services with the Hawaiʻi State Public Library System before visiting.

cards.title: Old Stadium Park
cards.subtitle: South King Street corridor
cards.notes: Plan around the short Wednesday market window if you want to see the park activated by the city’s People’s Open Market program.
cards.short_summary: Park venue for the Wednesday Old Stadium People’s Open Market.
cards.evidence_claim: Honolulu lists the Old Stadium People’s Open Market at Old Stadium Park, 2237 South King St., on Wednesdays from 8:15–9:15 a.m.
cards.source_title: City and County of Honolulu — Oʻahu Farmers Market Directory
cards.access_notes: The city directory gives Wednesday 8:15–9:15 a.m.; vendors and availability can vary.

cards.title: Mānoa Marketplace
cards.subtitle: Woodlawn Drive corridor
cards.notes: Use the Woodlawn Drive center as a practical errand stop, and check individual merchants for their own current hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Mānoa Marketplace lists its address as 2752 Woodlawn Drive and states that the center is open daily from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Center hours are 6 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; merchant hours vary.

cards.title: Mānoa Public Library
cards.subtitle: Woodlawn Drive corridor
cards.notes: Bring a task that benefits from free Wi‑Fi or a computer, and check the branch calendar before traveling for a program.
cards.short_summary: LEED Gold public library with Wi‑Fi and computers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hawaiʻi State Public Library System lists Mānoa Public Library at 2716 Woodlawn Dr. and identifies free Wi‑Fi and 18 computers.
cards.source_title: Hawaiʻi State Public Library System — Mānoa Public Library
cards.access_notes: The official branch page publishes daily hours, services, accessibility details, and an events calendar.

cards.title: Morning Glass Coffee
cards.subtitle: East Mānoa Road corridor
cards.notes: Make this a breakfast or lunch stop and use the official page to check the day’s kitchen window before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: Specialty-coffee café with house-made pastries, breakfast, and lunch.
cards.evidence_claim: Morning Glass Coffee lists 2955 East Mānoa Road and describes specialty coffee, house-made pastries, breakfast, and lunch.
cards.access_notes: Official hours vary by weekday and weekend; Monday is not listed among open days.

cards.title: Waioli Kitchen & Bake Shop
cards.subtitle: Mānoa Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow the restaurant’s Mānoa Road directions into the Salvation Army lot, then choose from its breakfast, lunch, or bakery menus.
cards.short_summary: Restaurant and bakery on the former Waioli Tea Room site.
cards.evidence_claim: Waioli Kitchen & Bake Shop states it is on the historic Waioli Tea Room site and provides directions to 2950 Mānoa Road.
cards.source_title: Directions to Waioli Kitchen & Bake Shop
cards.access_notes: The business directs visitors to turn into the Salvation Army driveway and then its parking lot.
